question: What attribution model works for a multi-touch enterprise sales motion?
answer:
**First-touch attribution for lead gen (did marketing generate the lead?), last-touch for close (which motion closed it?), multi-touch for pipeline (how many touches before deal materialized?). Don't pick one; use all three.** Enterprise deals have 5–9 touches over 6 months. Single-touch attribution will lie to you. **Why single-touch fails in enterprise:** A $500K deal touches marketing 7 times (content → webinar → whitepaper → nurture email), sales 3 times (cold call → demo → proposal). If you credit "last touch" (proposal), you ignore that marketing warmed the account. If you credit "first touch" (content), you ignore that sales closed it. Both teams think the other is useless. **The three models that work together:** 1. **First-touch attribution (for lead gen credit):** - How did the account first enter our funnel? Paid ad, content, webinar, cold call, inbound, partner? - Use: Measure marketing's ability to generate new account interest (not quality, just awareness). - Warning: "First touch" is often cheap. If 60% of first touches are ads, that's not genius; it's spend. - Formula: Assign 100% credit to first campaign that touched the account. 2. **Last-touch attribution (for sales motion credit):** - What motion closed the deal? Inbound motion, outbound direct, expansion, channel? - Use: Decide where to invest sales headcount (if expansion closes 40% of revenue, build that team). - Reality check: Don't let sales claim credit for a warm lead marketing built. That's a political fight; use the other models to settle it. - Formula: Assign 100% credit to the motion that closed the deal. 3. **Multi-touch attribution (the honest version):** - Split credit across all touches. Most common: 40% first, 40% last, 20% middle. - Use: Understand the full customer journey (marketing warms → sales demo → marketing whitepaper → sales closes). - Formula: Divide each touch by 5 (if 5 touches), multiply by weight (first = 40%, last = 40%, middle = 20% each). - Tools: Marketo, HubSpot, Salesforce Einstein, custom Tableau model. **In practice (realistic $20M ARR, 60% enterprise):** | Deal | First Touch | Mid Touches | Last Touch | Multi-Touch Credit | |------|------------|------------|-----------|-------------------| | $300K deal | Content (40%) | Email (20%) + Demo (20%) | Proposal (40%) | Content 40%, Email 10%, Demo 10%, Proposal 40% | | $100K deal | Paid Ad (40%) | Call (20%), Webinar (20%) | Negotiation (40%) | Paid Ad 40%, Call 10%, Webinar 10%, Negotiation 40% | **Operational implementation:** 1. **Define your stages:** - Awareness (first touch): How did they find you? - Evaluation (mid touches): Webinar? Cold call? Email sequence? - Decision (last touch): Who closed it? AE? Expansion manager? Partner? 2. **Log all touches in Salesforce** (one Activity record per touch, with Campaign). Without this, you can't run any model. 3. **Monthly dashboard:** Three columns for each deal. - First-touch source ("Which campaign first touched this account?") - Last-touch motion ("Which team closed it?") - Multi-touch path ("What was the customer journey?") 4. **Quarterly review:** "First touch tells us marketing is doing X. Last touch tells us sales is good at Y. Multi-touch tells us the journey is Z. Do we match?" If all three tell the same story (e.g., marketing-generated leads have 60% win rate, sales-generated have 40%), you're aligned. **Biggest trap:** "Let's use all three, but let [team] decide which one counts." Sales will always pick first-touch (to credit their outbound). Marketing will pick last-touch (to claim the close). Use a neutral party (CFO/RevOps) to define rules, then live with them for a full year. **Action:** Pick a model. Implement for 3 months. Don't change it. After 12 months, switch models and compare; you'll learn which one works best for YOUR company. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[Prospect] --> B[First Touch
